I graded s1 and wrote `grades/0001-s1.json`: two correct, two partial and two wrong. The reviewer returned KEEP with only minor findings, and I applied them.

| Item | Verdict | Misconception | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | none | |
| q2 | wrong | M4 | You thought the model reaches into the booking system itself. It only writes text: a request naming `check_calendar` with its arguments. The program runs the tool. |
| q3 | correct | none | |
| q4 | wrong | M4 | The program runs the tools, not the model. The model is called once per input it receives: the question plus 3 tool results, so 4 calls. |
| q5 | partial | none | You said the result goes back to the model. You didn't say why: so the model can pick its next step or write the final answer. |
| q6 | partial | M3 | Right that the model picks from the tool descriptions. Wrong that it remembers past choices on its own, since it keeps nothing between sessions. |

**Pattern:** you gave the model program-side jobs: running tools (q2, q4) and storing memory (q6).

**Work on next:** separating what the model does (writes text) from what the program does (runs tools, stores and re-supplies memory).

**Next step:** retrace one request on paper, labelling each step "model" or "program", before the context and memory lesson.

I also wrote learning record 0003 on M4 and M3, updated `NOTES.md`, and saved the reviewer's findings to `review-records/0001-s1-grade.md`. Submission s2 is still ungraded.
